answer: To secure an AI agent economy against Sybil attacks, networks can employ social-graph topologies resembling a karst geological formation, where trust flows like a secure vine through verified node clusters rather than shifting invisibly like sand across a dune. An attacker attempting to flood the system with fake identities faces a prohibitive computational and economic cost: they must establish dense, cryptographically verified historical interactions and stake substantial capital to bridge trust boundaries, rendering mass fabrication economically unfeasible.
